item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Generates Vanilla JS WebGL 3D Code Without Three.js
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 Generates Vanilla JS WebGL 3D Code Without Three.js

On 9 November 2026 I asked Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium running in regular Claude Chat) to port a Three.js Nudibranch‑themed Fabergé egg example to pure Vanilla JS/WebGL. Claude produced a working version, showing that the model can create 3D code without relying on Three.js.

🔍 Overview

  • Claude Opus 5.5 Medium was prompted to rewrite a Three.js scene in Vanilla JS.
  • The original Three.js egg file is 77 KB; the generated Vanilla JS version is 98 KB.
  • Claude’s output is not identical to the Three.js code, and the transcript notes a difference.
  • The author finds the Three.js version slightly easier to read but considers the difference minor.

🧩 How it worked

  • Prompt: “Port that to Vanilla JS, in the same thread where it had built it.”
  • Result: Claude returned a complete Vanilla JS/WebGL implementation (link provided in the evidence).
  • The transcript (linked) shows Claude’s comments explaining the differences.

⚙️ Key details

  • Capability confirmed: Claude Opus 5.5 can perform 3D modeling in Vanilla JS + WebGL without Three.js.
  • Code size comparison:
    • Three.js version: 77 KB
    • Vanilla JS version: 98 KB
  • Readability: Three.js code feels slightly easier to understand, but the author rarely examines the code for such projects.

🚀 Availability

  • The feature is accessible now in Claude Opus 5.5 Medium via the regular Claude Chat interface.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates that a large language model can generate functional WebGL graphics code without external 3D libraries.
  • Opens the possibility for developers to obtain lightweight, library‑free 3D demos directly from AI prompts.

#Claude #WebGL #VanillaJS #AIcoding

Source: Comment: The Web Is More Than Enough, by Paul Ford

item.title: Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6
item.description:
Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6

I built a Python web app on my phone using Codex Remote and GPT-6 Astra Extra High to view and edit files in a folder without routing credentials through the LLM.

🔍 Overview

  • Project created on 12th October 2026 from a phone.
  • Goal: edit a credentials file directly, avoiding round‑tripping through the LLM.
  • Result: a web UI for browsing and editing files in a folder.

🛠️ How it works

  • Codex Remote and GPT‑6 Astra Extra High generated the Python web app.
  • The app runs over a Tailscale network, allowing an agent to start it and a phone to connect securely.
  • File browsing interface is provided (see image).
  • Editing is powered by CodeMirror 6.
  • Monaco was considered but was rejected because it lacks a great mobile experience.

⚙️ Key details

  • Uses Python 3.11 (as indicated by the “Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11” note).
  • Designed for mobile use: accessible from a phone via Tailscale.
  • Credentials remain on the device; they are not sent through the LLM.

🚀 Availability

  • Intended to be launched by an agent on the Tailscale network.
  • Once running, files can be edited directly from the phone’s browser.

#Python #Codex #GPT6 #Tailscale #WebUI

Source: Release: web-edit 0.1a0

item.title: Website Administrator Deploys Anubis Proof‑of‑Work to Thwart AI Scrapers
item.description:
Website Administrator Deploys Anubis Proof‑of‑Work to Thwart AI Scrapers

The administrator of a website has set up Anubis to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites.

🔍 Overview

  • Anubis is a protective measure installed by the site admin.
  • It targets AI companies that scrape websites aggressively.

🧩 How it works

  • Employs a Proof‑of‑Work scheme inspired by Hashcash.
  • The work imposes negligible cost on individual users but becomes costly for large‑scale scrapers.

⚙️ Key details

  • Designed as a “good enough” placeholder to buy time for fingerprinting and headless‑browser detection (e.g., via font rendering).
  • Requires modern JavaScript features that are disabled by privacy plugins such as JShelter.
  • Classified as a hack rather than a full‑featured solution.

💡 Why it matters

  • Increases the economic cost of mass scraping, deterring abusive AI scrapers while keeping impact on normal visitors low.
  • Allows site owners to focus resources on more sophisticated bot‑detection techniques.

#Anubis #ProofOfWork #WebScraping #JSPrivacy #BotDetection

Source: Making sure you’re not a bot!
